blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights FastRoute, a scalable load-aware anycast routing architecture designed by Microsoft to improve their CDN supporting numerous popular online services. The paper demonstrates mature systems thinking by prioritizing simplicity and operational ease over marginal performance gains, avoiding complex designs that would increase implementation and maintenance burdens. The key insight is leveraging anycast routing with layered proxies and DNS services, where each FastRoute node operates independently. The system dynamically adjusts traffic routing by withdrawing or announcing BGP prefixes based on node health, and uses DNS-based CNAME redirects to manage overload without altering BGP topology. This approach ensures gradual traffic shifts and avoids abrupt changes for users. The design's effectiveness is validated by two years of real-world operation, handling incidents like proxy failures and traffic spikes without manual intervention.
paper_title: FastRoute: A scalable load-aware anycast routing architecture for modern CDNs
paper_abstract: Performance of online applications directly impacts user satisfaction. A major component of the user-perceived performance of the application is the time spent in transit between the user’s device and the application existing in data centers. Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) are typically used to improve user-perceived application performance through a combination of caching and intelligent routing via proxies. In this paper, we describe FastRoute, a highly scalable and operational anycastbased system that has significantly improved the performance of numerous popular online services. While anycast is a common technique in modern CDNs for providing high-performance proximity routing, it sacrifices control over the load arriving at any individual proxy. We demonstrate that by collocating DNS and proxy services in each FastRoute node location, we can create a highperformance, completely distributed system for routing users to a nearby proxy while still enabling the graceful avoidance of overload an any individual proxy. 1 David A. Maltz
